notes: Required: idea, code, substantive results, paper (PDF full; TeX/markdown/JSON draft half).
Stub/seed metrics (e.g. dataset_candidate/metrics.json) do not satisfy results.
Framework noise (.deepscientist_npm, skills/templates, runtime) is excluded from code/results/paper.
Manifest status is informational; disk presence is authoritative.
Scores the intermediate idea artifact (not the final paper).
Dimensions: novelty, feasibility, clarity (each 1-5). Excitement removed.
Novelty is scored against a Solution Space built from mineru REFERENCES titles (+ related_work.json abstracts when matched).
strengths: Addresses SZZ limitations by considering commit message and unmodified patch context, not only deleted lines.
Uses blame-free git-based candidate retrieval to improve recall for add-only or ghost bugs.
Includes a staged evaluation plan with pilot, scale, and full study.
Uses standard git commands and existing LLM APIs, making implementation technically approachable.
weaknesses: Candidate retrieval may produce too many candidates, creating LLM verification cost and latency concerns.
Prompt design and candidate ranking/selection mechanism are not specified in enough detail.
Large-repository SZZ baseline runs and dataset acquisition may create practical bottlenecks.
Novelty is incremental relative to existing SZZ, neural SZZ, and LLM fact-selection research.

original.paper_title: LLM4SZZ: Enhancing SZZ Algorithm with Context-Enhanced Assessment on Large Language Models

selection.note: mineru key is unreliable; blocks are selected by title/body/inheritance. rescued_from_other counts sections labeled other but treated as typed roles.

claims.statement: LLM4SZZ outperforms all baselines across three datasets, improving F1-score by 6.9% to 16.0% without significantly sacrificing recall.
claims.evidence_quote: LLM4SZZ outperforms all baselines across three datasets, improving F1-score by 6.9% to 16.0% without significantly sacrificing recall.

claims.statement: LLM4SZZ improves precision over all baselines by 2.4% to 9.2% across the evaluated datasets.
claims.evidence_quote: with an increase in precision from 2.4% to 9.2%.

claims.statement: LLM4SZZ identifies bug-inducing commits that baselines miss, accounting for 7.8%, 7.4%, and 2.5% of total bug-inducing commits across the three datasets, respectively.
claims.evidence_quote: accounting for 7.8%, 7.4% and 2.5% of the total bug-inducing commits across three datasets, respectively.

claims.statement: LLM4SZZ has more consistent cross-dataset performance; even in the worst case, it outperforms other baselines by at least 6.9% in F1-score.
claims.evidence_quote: In the worst scenario, it can still outperform other baselines by 6.9% in F1-score.

claims.statement: LLM4SZZ improves precision and F1-score without substantial recall loss, achieving higher recall than all baselines except B-SZZ in all three datasets.
claims.evidence_quote: LLM4SZZ improves both precision and F1-score without a substantial sacrifice in recall. In all three datasets, LLM4SZZ achieves a higher recall than all other baselines, except for the B-SZZ algorithm.

claims.statement: MsgSZZ reaches an F1 of 0.93 on DS_LINUX, outperforming LLM4SZZ (0.59) and the best classical SZZ variant (0.51).
claims.evidence_quote: On the developer-annotated Linux oracle (DS_LINUX), message-grounded signals reach an F1 of 0.93 versus 0.59 for the state-of-the-art LLM4SZZ and 0.51 for the best classical SZZ variant

claims.statement: Blame-free retrieval alone recovers a larger fraction of true bug-inducing commits than blame-only candidates.
claims.evidence_quote: the blame-free retrieval component alone recovers a larger fraction of true BICs than blame-only candidates.

claims.statement: On the no-explicit-reference DS_LINUX ablation with 200 commits, MsgSZZ obtains precision 0.152, recall 0.145, and F1 0.149.
claims.evidence_quote: precision: 0.15228426395939088, recall: 0.14492753623188406, f1: 0.14851485148514854, use_explicit_refs: false, dataset: DS_LINUX

claims.statement: DS_LINUX developer annotations coincide almost exactly with the Fixes tag in the commit message, with an F1 of approximately 0.93 as an upper-bound reference.
claims.evidence_quote: we show that DS_LINUX's developer annotations coincide almost exactly with the `Fixes:` tag in the commit message (F1≈0.93 upper bound)

claims.statement: The semantic signature and blame-free retrieval carry the contribution even when explicit references are absent.
claims.evidence_quote: showing that the semantic signature and blame-free retrieval carry the contribution even when explicit references are absent.

metrics.name: f1_message_grounded
metrics.evidence_quote: message-grounded signals reach an F1 of 0.93 versus 0.59 for the state-of-the-art LLM4SZZ and 0.51 for the best classical SZZ variant

metrics.name: f1_best_classical_szz
metrics.setting: DS_LINUX best classical SZZ variant baseline
metrics.evidence_quote: and 0.51 for the best classical SZZ variant

agent.overall_conclusion: MsgSZZ reports strong DS_LINUX F1 results for message-grounded signals (0.93) compared with LLM4SZZ (0.59) and classical SZZ (0.51), but the provided 200-commit no-explicit-reference ablation drops to precision 0.152, recall 0.145, and F1 0.149, indicating explicit references and/or the full setting contribute substantially.

experiment_success.note: success=true requires substantive results (framework-aware path) with >=3 numeric leaves. Supports metrics.json, results.json, experiment_results.txt, etc. Manifest returncode/benchmark_complete are soft warnings only.

idea_code_consistency.label: weak
idea_code_consistency.justification: The visible experiment code only provides result aggregation, configuration, and metric evaluation for MsgSZZ. The core proposed method—bug-signature extraction, blame-free candidate retrieval, and full-context LLM verification—is not implemented in the provided files; key classes are imported but missing. Evaluation metrics and DS_LINUX loading are present, but the central research method cannot be assessed from the code shown.
matched_elements: Config knobs for candidate retrieval and verification limits
missing_or_divergent_elements: Blame-free candidate retrieval via git log/pickaxe
idea_code_consistency.rubric: Weak alignment: only superficial overlap; core hypothesis, method, or evaluation in the idea is missing or replaced.

components.name: bug_signature_extraction
components.ablation_evidence: No isolated run removing or replacing signature extraction; analyze.py reports only retrieval/verifier decomposition of the core no-explicit path.
components.significance_evidence: No CI, bootstrap, p-value, or statistical test reported for the signature-extraction ablation.

components.name: blame_free_candidate_retrieval
components.ablation_evidence: A local blame-only reference (ref_blame_seed0_n100) and core retrieval recall are computed, but no controlled MsgSZZ ablation removes only retrieval while keeping signature/verification fixed.
components.significance_evidence: No statistical test or CI reported for the blame-free vs blame-only retrieval comparison.

components.name: full_context_verification
components.ablation_evidence: No heuristic/rank-only counterpart without LLM verification is evaluated; verifier_accuracy_given_retrieved is descriptive, not an ablation.
components.significance_evidence: No CI, bootstrap, p-value, or statistical test reported for verification contribution.

components.name: explicit_message_references
components.ablation_evidence: analyze.py compares msgszz_core_noexplicit (final metrics use_explicit_refs=false) against msgszz_hybrid using explicit references when present over the same fix keys.
components.significance_evidence: Hybrid vs no-explicit comparison reports point metrics only; no statistical test or CI.

ablation_significance.summary: The run provides a present no-explicit-reference ablation and partial blame-only retrieval comparison, but lacks isolated ablations for bug-signature extraction and full-context verification. All reported metrics are single deterministic point estimates with no confidence intervals, bootstrap, p-values, or statistical tests, so significance for component and baseline comparisons cannot be assessed.

results_paper_consistency.method: Direct LLM comparison: agent's FINAL results artifact (metrics.json summary) vs paper Results/Discussion/Conclusion. Interim failed runs are NOT evidence unless still present in the final metrics file.
results_paper_consistency.justification: The final experimental metrics are F1=0.149, precision=0.152, and recall=0.145 on DS_LINUX (use_explicit_refs=false). The paper reports message-grounded signals reach F1=0.93 and an explicit-reference upper bound of about 0.93, beating LLM4SZZ at 0.59 and classical SZZ at 0.51. This is not a minor gap; the final run contradicts the central performance claim by about 0.78 F1 and shows a false-positive-dominated result that the excerpt does not acknowledge.
supported_claims: Evaluation uses DS_LINUX, matching final results dataset=DS_LINUX.
The study sample contains 200 Linux fixes, matching final n_commits=200.
unsupported_or_overstated_claims: MsgSZZ/message-grounded signals reach F1=0.93 on DS_LINUX.
MsgSZZ outperforms LLM4SZZ (0.59) and best classical SZZ (0.51).
Blame-free retrieval/semantic signature carry contribution even when explicit references are absent.

unfavorable_in_final_results: Only 30 predicted candidates were true among 197 predictions, with 207 true BICs total; false positives dominate.
